title: Bigger magnifying glass: the 128 px frame is enlarged in-graph to 288 px instead of 224 px before the EfficientNet-B0 trunks, so Berlin's small structures (cars, roof edges, kerbs, tree crowns) reach the borrowed filters at a scale closer to the one their ImageNet invariance was learned on
hypothesis: Builds on experiment 15, the one input-scale change of this era and one of its largest single steps: resizing the 128 px frame in-graph to 224 px (the trunk's ImageNet resolution) took held-out truedop_2024 from 65.5% to 74.25% usable (mission 0.395 -> 0.293) with zero new parameters. Its reading was FixRes-style: the pretrained filters carry invariance at the object scales they were trained on, and a 1 m/px aerial frame shows structures far smaller than ImageNet objects (a car is ~4 px at 128, ~7 px at 224). That lever was pulled once and never revisited; every experiment since has kept 224. Meanwhile the remaining gap on the champion (exp 20: 93.0% usable, 0.75% false, 6.25% abstain on truedop_2024; 100%/0% on the three training photographs at the same viewpoints) is the survey gap, and the survey-invariance lever that has paid on this ruler is what the PRETRAINED TRUNK brings (MNV3-S -> MNV2 -> B0), not training-procedure invariance tricks (JS consistency exp 23, continuous vantages exp 22, patchwork exp 27, LP-FT exp 26, Noisy-Student weights exp 25 all failed to beat 0.0777). A bigger trunk is closed by the size gate (31.7 MB of 33.6 MB), but how much of the trunk's existing invariance reaches Berlin's fine structure is not: at 288 px the stride-16 read level becomes 18x18 (from 14x14) and stride-32 becomes 9x9 (from 7x7), so the 3x3 / 5x5 kernels of the early stages span ~1.3x less ground each and see small, survey-stable structure (street layout, building footprints, kerb lines) with more pixels, while survey-specific texture (shadow grain, canopy speckle, colour noise) is no sharper because upsampling adds no new information. Hypothesis: the limiting factor on the foreign photograph is that the trunk's scale-tuned invariance only partly engages on structures this small, and a further 1.29x enlargement engages more of it, lowering abstention without raising false fixes.
method: ONE change: INPUT_PX in model/model.py goes 224 -> 288 (2.25x enlargement of the 128 px frame, bilinear, in-graph, unchanged op). Everything that derives from it follows automatically: read levels become 112x18x18 (after features[5]) and 320x9x9 (after features[7]); GAP keeps the place feature at 112-d, so the parameter count, ONNX size and prototypes are identical. Trunk, MixStyle insertion points (after features[2]/[3]/[4], now 24x72x72 / 40x36x36 / 80x18x18), committee, cosine head, margin, offsets, decode, confidence gate, augmentation, 8 epochs, SWA from epoch 5 with BN recalibration: all unchanged.
expected_outcome: mission_score 0.0777 -> ~0.055-0.065 on truedop_2024: usable 93.0% -> ~94.5-95% (abstentions 25 -> ~17-20 frames), false fix held at <=1.0% (<=4 frames). Training-capture diagnostics stay ~100% usable / 0% false. Exported ONNX size unchanged (~31.7 MB); host latency rises ~1.6x (48.8 ms -> ~80 ms), well inside 250 ms; training wall-clock rises ~1.6x (~1.8 h -> ~3 h on the g6). If usable falls or stays flat while abstention moves only by noise (+/-2 frames = +/-0.005), the enlargement lever saturated at 224 and the scale reading of exp 15 is refuted beyond that point.
init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR — unchanged
eli5: The drone's camera picture is small, and the pre-trained 'eyes' we borrow were taught on everyday photos where things are big. Last time we blew the picture up to the size those eyes are used to, it was one of the biggest improvements so far. This time we blow it up a bit more, so cars, roof edges and street corners look less like specks and more like the shapes the eyes already know how to recognise in any lighting or season — without adding any memory to the drone.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: NOW: the 128 px frame is enlarged to 288 px (was 224) and read by two independent copies of EfficientNet-B0 (pre-trained on ImageNet, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned on Berlin; each reads a 112-channel 18×18 map (was 14×14) and a 320-channel 9×9 map (was 7×7), each lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame into a 112-number place description. The weights carried are the average of the many versions visited over the second half of training

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each); the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: unchanged from experiment 20: cross-survey style mixing, angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, 8 epochs, weight averaging from epoch 5 with normalisation statistics re-measured on 400 training batches

implementation_brief:
Single-constant change plus documentation; do NOT touch anything else.

model/model.py:
1. Change `INPUT_PX = 224` to `INPUT_PX = 288` and update its trailing comment (e.g. '# frame is bilinearly resized to this before the pretrained trunk: 2.25x enlargement, beyond ImageNet's 224 (exp 28)').
2. build_pretrained_trunk() already shape-checks with INPUT_PX // 16 and INPUT_PX // 32 (288 -> 18 and 9; both exact, 288 is divisible by 32) — leave the logic as is; just fix any comment text that hardcodes 224/14x14/7x7 (TRUNK_BLOCKS, TRUNK_OUT_CH, TRUNK_MID_BLOCKS comments, the MIXSTYLE_AFTER comment shapes become 24x72x72, 40x36x36, 80x18x18, Member docstring and the inline `# [B, 112, 14, 14]` / `# [B, 320, 7, 7]` comments -> 18,18 / 9,9).
3. Append a docstring section to the module docstring, after 'EFFICIENTNET-B0 TRUNK (experiment 19)', titled 'LARGER IN-GRAPH ENLARGEMENT (capture-holdout era, experiment 28)': the 128 px frame is now resized in-graph to INPUT_PX = 288 (2.25x) instead of 224, so the read levels are 112x18x18 and 320x9x9; no new parameters, GAP keeps the 112-d place feature, ONNX size unchanged; rationale = experiment 15's FixRes-style scale-matching step pushed further for Berlin's small aerial structures. Keep the existing NATIVE-SCALE INPUT (exp 15) section text as history.

model/train.py:
4. No logic change. MID_HW / DEEP_HW already derive from INPUT_PX (become 18 / 9). Update the comments that say '(14 at 224 px)' / '(7 at 224 px)' and the docstring line near line 86 that describes the 224 resize so they read 288 / 18 / 9 (add a one-line note 'experiment 28: 224 -> 288'). Keep BATCH_SIZE = 64, EPOCHS, AUG, MixStyle, SWA (AVG_EVERY, BN_RECAL_BATCHES, start epoch), learning rates and every other constant exactly as they are. If and only if a CUDA/MPS out-of-memory occurs at batch 64, do NOT shrink the batch silently — that would be a second change; instead keep 64 (bf16 autocast is already on for CUDA; two B0 members at 288 px x 64 fit comfortably in a 24 GB L4).
5. The train_info.json / log strings that interpolate INPUT_PX, MID_HW, DEEP_HW update by themselves; leave them.

Contracts to preserve (the frozen scorer depends on them):
- train.py CLI unchanged (same arguments, same defaults; reads only buckets(meta, "train") — nothing under model/ may open the truedop_2024 eval capture in any form).
- train.py exports one ONNX per area to <out>/models/<area>.onnx via model.export_onnx: input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1]; the 128->288 resize lives INSIDE the graph as the first op of Member.embed (F.interpolate bilinear, align_corners=False, fixed size), so the external input stays 128x128.
- Deployment gates (pipeline/score.py): fp32 ONNX <= 32 MiB (parameter count is unchanged, expect ~31.7 MB) and host latency proxy <= 250 ms (expect ~80 ms).
- Committee decode, confidence = min member block mass, export opset 17, dynamo=False — unchanged.
- Pretrained weights still load strict from model/pretrained/effb0_features7.pt; nothing is downloaded.
